name: Lactulose
meta: 10 g/15 mL (as listed: Lactulose solution, 200 mL)
Non-prescription / OTC category for this ingredient (combination may be Schedule H)
sections: Clear, colourless to brownish-yellow viscous liquid (solution); powder is white and freely soluble in water.

A synthetic disaccharide of galactose and fructose; on the WHO List of Essential Medicines. Laxative onset 8–48 hours. First approval/introduction: Medical use since the 1950s; for hepatic encephalopathy since 1966 (Bircher).
10 g/15 mL (as listed: Lactulose solution, 200 mL)

Synthetic disaccharide not absorbed in the small intestine; fermented by colonic bacteria to short-chain acids, lowering colonic pH. This draws water into the colon (laxative effect) and converts NH3 to non-absorbable NH4+, reducing blood ammonia in hepatic encephalopathy. Receptor / target profile: Osmotic action plus colonic acidification, which traps ammonia as ammonium and promotes growth of non-urease-producing bacteria.
Colonic bacterial fermentation to lactic, acetic and formic acids
Faeces (fermented); absorbed fraction in urine unchanged
Summary: Minimal systemic absorption (<3%); metabolised by colonic bacteria. Onset of laxative effect 24–48 h.
Faecal softening in haemorrhoids, post-anal surgery
Constipation (adults): 15–30 mL once or twice daily; adjust to 2–3 soft stools/day
Hepatic encephalopathy: 30–45 mL three to four times daily, titrated to 2–3 soft stools/day
May be mixed with water or juice; effect in 24–48 h
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
Main indication in encephalopathy; titrate to 2–3 soft stools.
GI obstruction, digestive perforation or risk of perforation
Contains galactose and lactose – caution in diabetes and lactose intolerance
Prolonged use – electrolyte imbalance; avoid excessive diarrhoea in hepatic encephalopathy
Other laxatives – may confound titration in encephalopathy
Mix with water/juice; contains small amounts of galactose/lactose.
Electrolytes on prolonged/high-dose use; stool frequency.
Diarrhoea, abdominal pain, fluid/electrolyte loss – stop and correct.
Sharma et al., Gastroenterology 2009 – lactulose prevented recurrence of hepatic encephalopathy.
Cochrane (Lee-Robichaud et al., 2010) – PEG superior to lactulose for chronic constipation.
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
